summary: Set 111 Session 3: decision rights and education mode. The decision-rights rubric from proposal SS11 is canonized in docs/ai-led-session-workflow.md: decisions route by WHOSE AUTHORITY they need, not by how much judgment they take, because in an AI-led workflow the operator usually lacks the surfaced context and a stop that asks them to adjudicate a judgment call is a context transfer they did not ask for. Four classes stay human -- external or hard-to-reverse consequences, underivable value trade-offs, accountability sign-offs, and the hard carve-out, anything that reduces verification. Everything judgment-shaped is AI-decidable under six ordered tiebreaks (goal over letter, prefer reversible, simpler code / fewer tests, defer to an existing gate, cross-provider consensus, human). The new ai_router.decision_journal is the blessed writer for a per-set decisions.jsonl carrying the question, decision, authority, the rubric line that fired, the options considered with each one's consequence and reversibility, and a MANDATORY no-default verification_effect; it REFUSES to write a 'reduces' record under AI authority and requires a non-empty operator_attestation on the operator's own. Education-mode briefs are canonized as the required format for any operator stop. Decision-time consensus is re-drawn as tiebreak 5 of the one rubric rather than a parallel mechanism with its own eligibility split, closing the laundering path where two engines agreeing appeared to create authority neither had.

reason.specifics: Session 4 is the ceremony pass -- artifact-necessity review, session-size cap, test-run policy, guided-look UAT, walk stager, guidance streamlining, CI hygiene -- and it is the set's terminal session, so it also owns Step 9 and the advisory path-aware critique. Every one of those items depends on context accumulated across S1-S3: which artifacts this set actually produced and read, which bounds were exercised, and which decisions were journaled. S4 also consumes this session's decisions.jsonl directly (the uat_decide filter feeds the walk's Decide section) and must weigh the structural recommendation S2 recorded about the unbounded close backstop. Cross-provider independence stays where it matters -- the session-verification route, which excluded anthropic and used gpt-5.5 for all three rounds this session. One carry-forward: S3 canonized the rubric that says a verification-REDUCING decision is operator-held, and S4's candidate list (bounding or narrowing the close backstop) is exactly such a decision, so it must arrive as an education-mode brief, not a self-authorized change.

notes: Verification loop actually run: discovery round 1 (K=2, both lenses, gpt-5.5, anthropic excluded) -> supplementary round 2 -> remediate once -> acceptance harness rounds 1 and 2 -> remediation-review round 3. Verdict VERIFIED, 2 fix verdicts accepted, 0 rejected, 0 findings. Both discovery passes spent; ONE of two remediation-review cycles used, so the loop closed inside its enforced bound with a cycle to spare. No operator authorization was needed or requested.

THE SUPPLEMENTARY ROUND CAUGHT THIS SESSION'S AUTHOR COMMITTING THE EXACT VIOLATION THE SESSION EXISTS TO PREVENT, and that is the most important thing this session produced. The first draft added decisions.jsonl to verification_stamp.WORK_DIFF_SET_BOOKKEEPING, which also removed the decision record from a --phase round's EVIDENCE bundle -- a reduction in verifier visibility, journaled as authority='ai' / verification_effect='none'. That is a self-authorized verification reduction, which the hard carve-out forbids outright. The round named it precisely and cited the journal's own record as the evidence.

The obvious fix was checked and REJECTED on evidence rather than preference. Simply reverting the bookkeeping entry would mean a post-round journal append changes work_diff_sha256, which invalidates the verification stamp (verification_stamp.py step 9); an invalid stamp sends the CLOSE BACKSTOP into a fresh round, and the close backstop has NO BOUND -- Session 2's record is six consecutive such rounds, every one a real metered dispatch recorded as $0.0000. Reverting would have traded a visibility defect for an unbounded-spend defect.

The actual defect was CONFLATING TWO CONSUMERS BEHIND ONE CONSTANT. Freshness asks 'did the reviewed work change after the stamp?' -- a record ABOUT the work can be exempt, because the code and doc changes the decision produced bind the diff on their own. Evidence asks 'what should the verifier read?' -- the AI-authority decision record is precisely what a reviewer should see. Fix: verification_stamp.EVIDENCE_VISIBLE_BOOKKEEPING names the entries that are freshness-exempt but stay visible, and PHASED_EVIDENCE_SET_EXCLUDES is DERIVED from WORK_DIFF_SET_BOOKKEEPING minus those, so the two lists cannot drift on any shared entry (L-069-1). verify_session.run() now imports the evidence list; the freshness digest and acceptance_evidence_is_stale() keep the freshness list, which is correct -- both are freshness consumers. The reduction is REMOVED, not authorized: no operator attestation was needed and none is claimed.

Round 1 (discovery, failure-scenario lens) found a second real defect: authority, rubric_line and verification_effect describe one decision from three angles, so a hand-assembled record could be individually well-formed and jointly false. The writer accepted rubric_line='verification-reduction' with verification_effect='none' and NO operator_attestation (the attestation requirement is keyed on the declared effect, so naming the carve-out while declaring no reduction walked straight past the only control it has), and accepted rubric_line='escalate-to-human' under authority='ai' (escalate-to-human is structurally the sixth AI tiebreak but semantically IS the escalation, so an operator stop would be journaled as an AI call). validate_record() now enforces three coherence rules, with the AI-authority carve-out check still ordered first so authority='ai' + verification-reduction keeps raising VerificationReductionRefused rather than a generic ValueError.

A THIRD defect was found by RUNNING the loop rather than by reviewing it, in Session 2's parser. The round-1 criterion arrived as a single backticked span whose content began with the JUDGMENT marker -- which is how the template's own 'JUDGMENT - <sentence>' example reads -- and verification._parse_acceptance only honoured the marker OUTSIDE the backticks. It parsed as executable, so the harness tried to run a prose sentence. It failed closed (outcome 'error', finding stays blocking, no false closure), so this is Minor by the L-095-1 consequence rubric, but it mislabels every judgment criterion written in the template's suggested style and spends a harness run establishing nothing. The marker now wins from inside the backticks too, with a reproduction of the exact round-1 criterion and a guard that ordinary backticked commands still parse executable.

S2's OWED RESIDUAL IS DISCHARGED. Session 2 closed via operator-attested --manual-verify with two fixes (close-backstop round 9, stale acceptance evidence; round 10, baseline-mismatch) carrying tests but no routed cross-provider verdict. They were named explicitly in s3-conventions.md under a PLEASE REVIEW heading, with file and function pointers and an invitation to find fault. Three routed rounds read that block and returned no finding against either. That is a real cross-provider verdict on both, and the residual is closed rather than carried forward.

Acceptance harness: 0 auto-closures across both findings-bearing rounds, both fail-closed and both correct. Round 1's criterion returned 'error' (a JUDGMENT sentence handed to the runner -- the parser defect above). Round 2's returned 'criterion-changed', because fixing that parser changed how the raw artifact re-parses, so the envelope's contract no longer matched the immutable raw artifact. The guard refusing to auto-close a criterion whose contract moved is exactly the S2 design working; both findings were settled by the remediation-review instead, which is where they belonged.

The journal was DOGFOODED on this session's own seven judgment-shaped calls, all through the blessed writer. Two of them are SUPERSEDING records appended after the verification rounds -- the journal is append-only and the original wrong call about bookkeeping placement was NOT edited. An audit trail showing a wrong decision being caught by verification and corrected is worth more than a tidy ledger, and it is the first live demonstration that the operator-as-auditor model surfaces what it is supposed to.

AGENTS.md went 113 tokens over its preload ceiling when the pointer landed. Ceilings ratchet down only and a raise is operator-authorized, so prose was CUT instead: the pointer shrank to a true pointer because the constitution is also preload and already carries the summary, making the long form duplication between two always-loaded files. All four preload files are green (constitution 88%, project-guidance 100%, lessons-learned 91%, AGENTS.md 99%; total 93% of the 12,000-token ceiling).

Suite: 3,658 passed / 0 failed / 10 skipped, full run of record after the last code change, with NOTHING deselected or excused. Targeted after the last code change: test_decision_journal.py + test_acceptance_harness.py -> 145 passed.

Deferred to Session 4 by the spec, not by omission: the ceremony pass -- artifact-necessity review (which must decide whether ai-assignment.md and sN-conventions.md survive at all), session-size cap, canonical test-run policy, guided-look UAT, walk stager, guidance streamlining, CI hygiene. S4 is also the set-terminal session, so it owns Step 9 and the advisory path-aware critique. requiresUAT is a set-level flag S4 dogfoods; S3 ships no UI surface, which is why requiresE2E is false and S3 owes no walk.

RECORDED FOR A FUTURE SET, NOT BUILT HERE: operator-notes.md gains a 2026-08-07 section on in-session progress visibility. The framework has a good SET-level surface (print_session_set_status, the Work Explorer tree) and NO step-level surface -- once a session is in flight the operator cannot see where in the process it is, even though activity-log.json's log_step entries are exactly that data, written as the session runs and rendered nowhere. GitHub Copilot CLI has no built-in checklist equivalent to Claude Code's, so this is either an orchestrator convention (adopted immediately: post a compact checklist at each phase transition, zero code, works on every engine) or a Work Explorer feature (expand an in-flight session node to show its logged steps). Same sequencing caveat as the other Explorer items: S4's artifact-necessity pass may reshape activity-log.json, so decide what survives before building a UI that renders it.

STRUCTURAL POINT INHERITED FROM S2 AND STILL OPEN, restated because S4 owns it: verify_session is bounded and the bound worked again this session (the loop closed with a cycle to spare), but the CLOSE BACKSTOP has no bound and never runs in GitHub CI, so its entire cost lands on the operator machine at close time. Bounding or narrowing it is a VERIFICATION-REDUCING decision and therefore operator-held under the rubric this session just canonized -- S4 must present it as an education-mode brief, not decide it.
